text: Why OpenAPI4s? The OpenAPI document stays the source of truth. OpenAPI4s generates idiomatic Scala 3 models, validation types, server routes and clients, then semantically merges later contract changes into those sources without replacing handwritten implementations. New fields, constraints, polymorphic cases and endpoints arrive through regeneration; application logic stays where you wrote it. The generated code is the integration layer, not another runtime abstraction. http4s output is ordinary http4s code and Sharaf output is ordinary Sharaf code. There is no additional endpoint DSL or layer of schema, codec and server-interpreter implicits to understand. That keeps the result simple for maintainers and makes it especially approachable for coding agents: inspect normal Scala files, fill the explicit ???, compile, test and regenerate. Regeneration preserves the code you wrote. Guardrail and template generators such as OpenAPI Generator or Swagger Codegen keep regeneration safe by treating generated transport code as disposable and putting user logic behind a separate interface. OpenAPI4s instead updates readable project sources in place. You can review a contract change and its direct Scala impact together. Tapir is an excellent Scala-first choice: Scala owns the endpoint description and OpenAPI is derived from it. OpenAPI4s is usually simpler when OpenAPI already owns the contract because it does not require recreating that contract in a Scala endpoint DSL. If Scala should own the contract, choose a Scala-first library. If OpenAPI should own it and generated code should remain editable, OpenAPI4s offers the shortest path from contract to native framework code. The trade-off is deliberate: merging is additive, so removals and renames need human cleanup, and unsupported features may produce an explicit TODO instead of a complete abstraction.
title: Why OpenAPI4s?

text:
Generate an http4s API with Iron Use Circe models with the http4s server backend and Iron validation: cs launch --scala-version 2.13.16 ba.sake::openapi4s-cli:0.9.0 \
  -M ba.sake.openapi4s.cli.OpenApi4sMain -- \
  --models circe \
  --framework http4s \
  --validation iron \
  --url openapi.yaml \
  --baseFolder src/main/scala \
  --basePackage com.example.api
 Add the generated-code dependencies to your application: //> using scala 3.9.0
//> using dep org.http4s::http4s-ember-server:0.23.38
//> using dep org.http4s::http4s-dsl:0.23.38
//> using dep org.http4s::http4s-circe:0.23.38
//> using dep io.circe::circe-generic:0.14.17
//> using dep io.github.iltotore::iron:3.4.1
//> using dep io.github.iltotore::iron-circe:3.4.1
 Implement the ??? bodies in the generated routes, then mount them in your server: import cats.effect.{IO, IOApp}
import com.comcast.ip4s.*
import com.example.api.routes.UsersRoutes
import org.http4s.ember.server.EmberServerBuilder
import org.http4s.implicits.*
import org.http4s.server.middleware.ErrorHandling

object Main extends IOApp.Simple:
  val run: IO[Unit] =
    val routes = ErrorHandling.httpRoutes[IO](new UsersRoutes().routes)
    EmberServerBuilder
      .default[IO]
      .withHost(host"127.0.0.1")
      .withPort(port"8080")
      .withHttpApp(routes.orNotFound)
      .build
      .useForever
 Iron constraints are enforced while Circe decodes the request body. Invalid JSON is a 400 Bad Request; structurally valid JSON that violates an Iron constraint is a 422 Unprocessable Entity. The generated error handling supplies those client-facing responses. Generated query matchers follow http4s route semantics: a missing required or malformed query parameter does not match the route and normally results in 404 Not Found.
title: Generate an http4s API with Iron

text: Regenerate an evolving API Run the same OpenAPI4s command whenever the contract changes. The generator parses the existing Scala source and merges additive changes into it. For a realistic change: Generate the initial API. Replace generated ??? route bodies with application logic. Add a schema field and an operation to the OpenAPI document. Run the original generation command again. Compile and exercise both the old and new routes. The existing method body remains yours. New model fields, cases and route methods are added. A new endpoint initially contains ???, making the missing implementation explicit at compile or runtime rather than silently inventing behavior. Incremental generation is additive. Renames and removals are not destructive migrations: review and remove obsolete Scala code yourself. Commit generated sources so an ordinary code review shows both contract evolution and its Scala impact.
title: Regenerate an evolving API

text: Backends and dependencies Choose one model backend, an optional server backend, an optional validation backend and an optional client backend. Purpose Backend Compatibility Models circe http4s, sttp and Iron Models tupson Sharaf, sttp and Validson Server http4s Use with Circe models Server sharaf Use with Tupson models Validation iron Use with Circe models Validation validson Use with Tupson models Client sttp Use with Circe or Tupson models Generated-code compilation is tested on Scala 3.9.0. Generated code Dependencies Tupson models ba.sake::tupson:0.31.0, ba.sake::validson:0.20.0 Circe models io.circe::circe-core:0.14.17, io.circe::circe-generic:0.14.17 Sharaf controllers ba.sake::sharaf:0.9.3 http4s routes org.http4s::http4s-dsl:0.23.38, plus http4s-circe for Circe models Iron validation io.github.iltotore::iron:3.4.1, iron-circe:3.4.1 sttp clients com.softwaremill.sttp.client4::core:4.1.0, plus the selected JSON integration The Mill plugin and sbt plugin expose equivalent build settings.

text:
CLI All runs generate models. Add --framework for a server or --client for a client. Flag Default Description --models tupson Model backend: circe or tupson --framework none Server backend: http4s or sharaf --validation none Validation backend: none, iron or validson --client none Client backend: sttp --tags none Comma-separated operation tags to include --excludeTags none Comma-separated tags to exclude; wins over --tags --serverTags, --serverExcludeTags none Server-only tag overrides --clientTags, --clientExcludeTags none Client-only tag overrides --url openapi.json OpenAPI URL/path, JSON Schema HTTP(S) URL, file, or directory --baseFolder src/main/scala Generated source directory --basePackage required Package for generated sources Generated sources land below <baseFolder>/<basePackage path>/ in models, controllers, routes and clients, depending on the selected backends. Snapshots Add https://central.sonatype.com/repository/maven-snapshots as a repository, then launch the snapshot explicitly: cs launch --scala-version 2.13.16 \
  -r https://central.sonatype.com/repository/maven-snapshots \
  ba.sake::openapi4s-cli:0.9.1-SNAPSHOT \
  -M ba.sake.openapi4s.cli.OpenApi4sMain -- --help
 Use the snapshot version reported by the main-branch CI job. Tagged releases are published to Maven Central.
title: CLI

text: Limitations Payload generation is JSON-only. JSON Schema input is model-only. It may be one .json file, a directory of schemas, or a single HTTP(S) URL. Remote schemas are fetched without authentication, resolve references against the document URL (not $id), and may only reference other HTTP(S) schemas. Incremental generation is additive; it does not automatically delete Scala code after contract removals or renames. http4s query parameters use typed DSL matchers. Unsupported decoder types such as UUIDs, dates and named enums receive one explicit given QueryParamDecoder[T] = ??? to implement. Missing required or malformed http4s query parameters do not match the route, following http4s DSL behavior. Non-repeated array query encodings and query-parameter schema validation are not implemented. The sttp backend does not yet generate auth/security schemes, multipart bodies, streaming, or non-JSON content types.
title: Limitations

text:
Quickstart This tutorial generates Scala 3 models and http4s routes from a small OpenAPI contract. 1. Create the contract Save this as openapi.yaml: openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Users API
  version: 1.0.0
paths:
  /users/{id}:
    get:
      tags: [Users]
      operationId: getUser
      parameters:
        - name: id
          in: path
          required: true
          schema:
            type: integer
            format: int64
      responses:
        "200":
          description: A user
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/User"
components:
  schemas:
    User:
      type: object
      required: [id, name]
      properties:
        id:
          type: integer
          format: int64
        name:
          type: string
 2. Run the generator cs launch --scala-version 2.13.16 ba.sake::openapi4s-cli:0.9.0 \
  -M ba.sake.openapi4s.cli.OpenApi4sMain -- \
  --models circe \
  --framework http4s \
  --url openapi.yaml \
  --baseFolder src/main/scala \
  --basePackage com.example.api
 OpenAPI4s creates the models and routes packages below com.example.api. Route methods deliberately contain ???: you fill in the implementation. 3. Implement and regenerate Replace the generated placeholder in UsersRoutes with your application logic. When the contract gains a field or endpoint, run the same command again. OpenAPI4s adds the new generated structure while preserving your implementation. Next, generate an http4s API with Iron validation, or consult the CLI reference for other backends.
title: Quickstart
